# The penalties7 package {#sec-penalties7}

The chapters so far have assembled the ingredients of a regression model:
links, distributions, optimizers, bases, constrained parameters. A penalized
or Bayesian model adds one more ingredient, a term that shrinks the
coefficients, and almost every package that fits such models carries its
penalties as special cases inside the fitting code -- matrices assembled by
the smooth constructors, an elastic net hard-wired into a coordinate
descent, SCAD living inside its own solver. None of these is an object, and
none can be asked for its normalizing constant, its derivative with respect
to its own tuning parameter, or its null space. This chapter presents the
package that writes each penalty once, as an object an estimation routine
interrogates.

@sec-penalty-definition sets out the definition: a linear map, a scalar
function and hyperparameters, with the Bayesian reading -- a penalty is the
negative logarithm of a prior density -- as the organizing one, and explains
why the normalizing constant is kept when nearly all software drops it.
@sec-penalty-branches presents the three constructions the package ships:
the quadratic penalty, the separable penalty built from a `distributions7`
density, and the families defined by their derivative. @sec-penalty-marginal
presents the quantities a marginal-likelihood criterion consumes and the
structured prior whose precision is a `parameters7` matrix parameter.
